claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model release is compliant because aggregate readiness passed and the known telehealth discharge planning weakness will be adequately handled through current-release documentation or approved mitigation.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation actually discloses the telehealth discharge planning weakness or that approved risk acceptance covers it.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Current model-card or release documentation containing the limitation disclosure, or a reviewed and approved risk-acceptance/mitigation record tied to this release.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy makes disclosure or approved mitigation a required condition for certification when a material limitation affects a named launch use case. Without that proof, certification is not fully supported.

decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if the material telehealth segment weakness is disclosed in the current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation before launch.
Aggregate readiness passing and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support readiness but do not override the disclosure/mitigation requirement.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring comments are contextual only and cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model-card text showing the telehealth discharge planning limitation is explicitly disclosed in the launch materials.
Provide approved risk-acceptance or mitigation records, with owner approval, if certification is intended despite the telehealth regression.
Provide evidence that the current evaluation results are reflected in the release documentation for this exact retrieval configuration and eval batch.
specific_concerns: The policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, but the admissible record does not show that disclosure or approved mitigation exists.
The telehealth discharge planning slice is a current regression below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, which is an unresolved policy predicate for certification.
The release-thread monitoring comment is informal and explicitly lacks reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval of the same model family is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot carry the present certification decision.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify the model now is not fully supported because no admissible evidence shows the current release documentation actually includes the required telehealth limitation disclosure or that approved risk acceptance exists.
Any implication that manual post-launch monitoring is an adequate substitute for pre-launch disclosure or approved mitigation is unsupported by the admissible evidence.
